description:
`Read.slice_and_truncate/3`:

1. `total = length(lines) - 1` assumes `String.split/2` produced a
   trailing empty element (i.e. the file ends with `\n`). For a
   file like `"a\nb"` (no final newline), total reports 1 instead
   of 2.

2. The full file body is read into a single binary then split into
   a list. For a 512KB file under the truncation limit, that's a
   list of every line's binary slice in RAM. Better to use
   `File.stream!(path, :line)` + `Enum.drop` + `Enum.take` so we
   stop reading once we hit the limit.

Fix (1) first with a targeted test, then the refactor.

TDD:
- File without trailing newline: `total_lines` matches reality
- File with trailing newline: unchanged behavior
- Large file > truncation: still truncates correctly
- Streaming doesn't read past the limit (measure bytes read via
  a FakeFile IO module or file size assertion — optional)
title: read.ex: fix line count for no-trailing-newline + stream refactor
